headline: A stormy week: rounds of rain, gusty winds, mountain snow and coastal flooding, starting with minor coastal flooding on the Strait of Juan de Fuca shore until 2 PM today and steadier rain tonight, then heavier rain Wednesday night into Thursday that could push the Skokomish River to moderate flood stage.

sections.title: Today & Tonight
sections.text: Light showers stream in Monday, mainly along the coast and over the Olympics with a few reaching the Sequim–Port Angeles area and the Puget Sound lowlands, before steadier rain arrives Monday evening as the next front moves in. Highs are near normal, in the upper 40s to near 50. A Coastal Flood Advisory covers the Strait of Juan de Fuca shore until 2 PM for minor flooding around the high tide. Snow levels near 2,000–3,000 feet give the Olympics 4–8 inches under a Winter Weather Advisory until 4 PM, then rise to 3,000–4,500 feet tonight; a Wind Advisory for gusts to 40 mph starts at 4 PM for the coast and the western and southern Olympic foothills.

sections.title: Short Term
sections.text: Tuesday brings widespread rain and southeast winds; around Seattle a few gusts near 23 mph are possible, mainly Tuesday morning, while the coastal Wind Advisory runs until 4 PM Tuesday. Rain tapers Tuesday afternoon with highs in the low 50s, and snow levels rise to around 5,000 feet: Stevens Pass may get 1–3 inches and the North Cascades (such as Washington Pass) 4–8 inches, with a Winter Weather Advisory for the Whatcom and Skagit County Cascades from 8 PM tonight to 10 PM Tuesday. Tides run noticeably higher along the Strait and Puget Sound shorelines from Tuesday on, and forecasters are watching closely for flooding there. Another front arrives Wednesday with more widespread lowland rain, breezy winds and mountain snow.

sections.title: Long Term
sections.text: The heaviest rain of the week is expected Wednesday night into Thursday, especially over the Olympics, where the Skokomish River is forecast to reach moderate flood stage; a Hydrologic Outlook is out, though no widespread river flooding is expected. High pressure is favored to rebuild late in the week, making Friday a break from the wind before it turns breezy again over the weekend.

coast: A Coastal Flood Warning covers the Grays Harbor County coast until 2 PM today for moderate to major flooding at the high tide, especially in Westport and Ocean Shores, and a Coastal Flood Advisory covers the north coast and the Strait of Juan de Fuca until 2 PM for minor flooding. Confidence is growing in moderate to major coastal flooding again on the Grays Harbor coast with Wednesday's tides, possibly made worse by high surf, and tides rise along the Strait and Puget Sound from Tuesday on. For boaters, a Storm Warning covers the outer coastal waters (10–60 miles out) until 3 PM Tuesday for southeast gusts up to about 63 mph (55 knots); Gale Warnings cover the inner coastal waters and the east Strait entrance for gusts up to about 46 mph (40 knots); and Small Craft Advisories cover the central and west Strait, Admiralty Inlet, the northern inland waters and San Juan Islands, and the Grays Harbor bar, with winds about 23–35 mph (20–30 knots). Another front Wednesday into Thursday brings possible storm-force gusts on the coastal waters, gales on the east Strait and north waters, and a 30 percent chance of thunderstorms offshore. Seas of 10–12 feet today build to 18–22 feet Tuesday through Thursday, then ease to 10–12 feet Friday through the weekend; rough Grays Harbor bar conditions may become severe midweek.
watch_for: Higher tides along the Strait of Juan de Fuca and Puget Sound shorelines from Tuesday on, after today's minor coastal flooding on the Strait.
Heavy rain Wednesday night into Thursday, with the Skokomish River forecast to reach moderate flood stage.
Moderate to major coastal flooding again on the Grays Harbor coast with Wednesday's high tides.
confidence: Forecasters are confident in the wet, windy pattern through Thursday and increasingly confident in Wednesday's Grays Harbor coastal flooding, while tide impacts on the Strait and Puget Sound and the late-week details are still being monitored.
